issues.description: The problem statement (and the commented example in Main.java) refers to a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int), but the solution implements a static method with a different name (receiveDelivery(String, int, int)). This name mismatch between the specification/example and the provided solution will confuse students about the required API and cause inconsistencies when following the example code in Main.java.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either rename the solution method receiveDelivery(...) to acceptSupplyDelivery(...), or update the problem statement and Main.java example to use receiveDelivery(...). Ensure all references and tests (if any) use the same method name and signature.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template's example use the method name acceptSupplyDelivery(...) to describe receiving ingredient deliveries, but the solution implementation names this method receiveDelivery(...). This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual operation (accepting a supply delivery and updating the shared stock) creates a mapping barrier: students reading the problem and template will look for acceptSupplyDelivery, while the reference implementation provides receiveDelivery.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent method name across all artifacts. Rename the solution's receiveDelivery(...) method to acceptSupplyDelivery(...), preserving its static signature and behavior (or alternatively update the problem statement and template examples to call receiveDelivery). This makes the conceptual mapping explicit and removes unnecessary confusion.
